data.title: STOCKS | Morgan Stanley Adds 15 Names to Its Europe Core Overweight List
data.description:
Morgan Stanley's strategy team made an unusually large overhaul of its high-conviction stock pool, recommending that investors broaden their exposure in European portfolios rather than focus only on market themes such as AI capital spending and defense. According to Sina Finance, the team led by Marina Zavolock said it favors a diversified allocation strategy rather than abandoning the AI investment theme.

Since the end of August, the team has added 15 overweight top picks, compared with the usual monthly addition of three to four names. The list now includes 43 overweight top picks, 60% of which were added over the past three months. The new additions span banks and financials, including ABN AMRO Bank, Lloyds Banking Group, Arden, and EQT; companies with their own stock-specific logic such as Accor, Shell, and Scout24; and firms benefiting from artificial intelligence and data center development, including Legrand, Kingspan, and Merlin Properties.

data.title: STOCKS | BofA Survey: Investors Still Bullish on Macro and AI Capex
data.description: A Bank of America survey showed investors still believe in improving macroeconomic conditions and rapid growth in artificial intelligence capital spending, but risks from a disorderly surge in bond yields and a Democratic landslide in the midterm elections have made market sentiment more cautious. According to Sina Finance, a strategist team led by Michael Hartnett wrote that the September Global Fund Manager Survey showed cash allocations rose from 3.5% to 3.9%, the biggest monthly increase since March, as excessive summer optimism faded. The report said risk exposure is appropriate only when cash allocations return to the neutral 4% to 5% range. Investors' net underweight in bonds reached 48%, the highest since May 2022, while the net overweight in stocks fell to 49% from 56% in the previous month.

data.title: Southern Philippines Regional Vote Points To No Majority
data.description: According to Nikkei Asia, initial results from the historic election for a regional assembly in the separatist-wracked southern Philippines indicate that no party is set to win a majority in the 80-seat parliament.

data.title: Marsh Lifts Treasury Weighting to Neutral as Yields Stay Elevated
data.description:
US investment consultancy Marsh is raising Treasury allocations in some portfolios it recommends to clients, according to Bloomberg.

The move reflects large investors’ efforts to take advantage of elevated yields.

data.title: AI | JPMorgan’s Sundar Says AI Trade Is in ‘Digestion’ Phase
data.description:
Sitara Sundar, head of alternative investment strategy at JPMorgan Private Bank, said the artificial intelligence trade is in a “digestion” phase and that the firm remains constructive on the AI industry over the long run, according to Bloomberg.

Speaking on Bloomberg Television, Sundar said JPMorgan would lean more into the integration and application layers of artificial intelligence.

data.title: Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi To Visit China On September 16
data.description:
China's Foreign Ministry said Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi will visit China on September 16, and Foreign Minister Wang Yi will hold talks with him, according to ETNet.

This will be Araghchi's second visit to China this year and comes ahead of the planned meeting between Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump. ETNet reported that Araghchi's previous visit in early May was his first trip to China since the U.S.-Iran conflict escalated, and that he briefed Wang on the latest status of U.S.-Iran talks and Iran's next steps.

data.title: AI TRENDS | Gates Foundation Plans at Least $1 Billion to Expand AI Access
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, the Gates Foundation plans to invest at least $1 billion over the next two years to improve access to artificial intelligence, and co-founder Bill Gates warned that the way AI is spread could widen the global wealth gap further. In a report, Gates wrote that if AI is properly guided, it will give more people solutions, opportunities, and knowledge that have long been out of reach, and that decisions over the next 12 to 18 months on how AI is built, funded, and deployed will determine whether the technology mainly benefits those with the most resources or reaches those with the least. The Gates Foundation plans to donate a cumulative $200 billion before it closes in 2045.

data.title: MediaTek Launches Dimensity 9600 Pro Flagship Chip on 2nm Process
data.description:
MediaTek unveiled its next-generation flagship chip, the Dimensity 9600 Pro, at its 2026 Dimensity flagship product launch on September 15. According to ChainCatcher, the chip uses TSMC's 2nm process and contains more than 33 billion transistors.

The company said the chip adopts a fused computing architecture that integrates CPU, GPU, NPU, and ISP cores around AI. It features an all-big-core design with two C2-Ultra cores at 4.55GHz, three C2-Pro cores at 4.35GHz, and three C2-Pro cores at 3.1GHz, along with 34.5MB of L2+L3+ system cache. It also supports LPDDR6 memory and UFS 5.0 storage.

MediaTek said the Dimensity 9600 Pro's big-core power consumption is down 37% and multi-core power consumption is down 61% versus the Dimensity 9500. In GeekBench V6.4, it scored 4,276 in single-core and 12,650 in multi-core tests, up about 17% and 15%, respectively, from the Dimensity 9500. The NPU uses a dual-NPU architecture with the APU 1090, and peak performance is said to be up 51%. MediaTek also said it has ranked first in global smartphone SoC market share for six consecutive years.

data.title: Finloop Raises Over $10 Million in A+ Round and Launches Enterprise Wealth Service
data.description:
Finloop Finance Technology has completed an A+ funding round of more than $10 million, with HSBC and People's Capital among the investors. According to Foresight News, Finloop also launched a one-stop enterprise wealth management service called Finterprise to provide digital solutions for corporate clients' cash and liquidity management needs.

Finloop describes itself as a Hong Kong-based AI-driven global Web5 (Web2+Web3) wealth technology platform. It says it provides wealth management products and technology solutions for financial institutions across cash management, mutual funds, alternative investments, structured products, bonds, insurance and virtual assets.

data.title: ASIA MARKET CLOSE | Hong Kong Slips 1% and Korea Falls a Fourth Day on Chip, Rate Jitters; Nikkei Flat
data.description:
According to RTHK, HKET and Yonhap, Asian equities closed mostly lower on Tuesday as a fresh climb in U.S. bond yields and a selloff in chip and memory names pressured the region.

Tokyo's Nikkei 225 finished virtually unchanged at 63,484.10, down 8.89 points or 0.01%, after a choppy session that spanned a range of more than 1,030 points. Chip-related names lagged, with Advantest down 2.96% and Tokyo Electron off 0.55%, while Sony fell 1.66%.

Seoul's KOSPI ended down 0.85% at 6,627.26, its fourth straight losing session, as the won weakened against the dollar amid rising bond yields. Bank of Korea minutes pointed to a possible policy rift over back-to-back rate hikes. Samsung Electronics eased 0.20% and SK Hynix slipped 0.41%.

Hong Kong stocks retreated, with the Hang Seng Index closing down 1.00% at 24,667.24 and the Hang Seng Tech Index off about 0.6% at 4,291; turnover reached HK$187.2 billion. Tencent bucked the trend to rise about 1.9% and Alibaba added more than 1%, while Lenovo fell nearly 3%, Zhipu dropped about 5% and MINIMAX declined 7%.

Taiwan's TAIEX closed down 351.03 points or 0.77% at 45,511.49 on thin turnover of NT$603.5 billion, as memory and chip stocks bore selling pressure. TSMC rose NT$5 or 0.21% to NT$2,385, while MediaTek fell 2.85% and Hon Hai eased 0.80%.

In mainland China, the Shanghai Composite closed down 0.54% at 3,864.28, its fourth straight decline, and the ChiNext Index fell 1.15% to 3,247.92, with A-share turnover holding near a year-to-date low.

data.title: Iranian Foreign Minister Meets PUK Leader in Tehran
data.description: According to Sina Finance, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said in a post that he met with Patriotic Union of Kurdistan leader Bafel Talabani in Tehran on Tuesday.

data.title: Xingqi Ophthalmic Drug Wins China NMPA Approval for SQ-25012 Thyroid Eye Disease Trial
data.description: Xingqi Ophthalmic Drug said on September 15 that it received China's National Medical Products Administration approval notice for SQ-25012 injection, allowing the company to begin a clinical trial for thyroid eye disease, according to Jiemian News. The drug is a recombinant humanized IgG1 trispecific antibody and is classified as a category 1 innovative biologic medicine for treatment. Xingqi said it has completed pharmaceutical and non-clinical pharmacology and toxicology studies, which showed good safety and clinical development value. As of the announcement date, no drug of the same type has been approved for marketing.

data.title: China's SAMR, Culture and Tourism Ministry Warn Online Hotel Booking Platforms to Curb Competition Risks
data.description:
China's State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and the Ministry of Culture and Tourism held an administrative guidance meeting on online hotel booking platform services on September 15, telling Meituan, Douyin, JD.com, Trip.com, Tongcheng and Fliggy to strictly fulfill compliance responsibilities and prevent competition risks, according to Jiemian News. The meeting said fair competition is the legal foundation of a market economy and that compliance is essential for business development.

The regulators said online hotel booking platforms have grown rapidly in recent years and have helped make travel more convenient and support tourism spending, but competition risks should not be ignored. They urged platform companies to abide by China's Anti-Monopoly Law, Anti-Unfair Competition Law, E-Commerce Law and Tourism Law, conduct self-inspections, and avoid exclusive cooperation arrangements and "lowest price across the internet" practices. The meeting also called for stronger compliance systems, healthier competition and better protection of consumer rights.

data.title: STOCKS | M&S Grocery Sales Surge as Cyberattack Impact Eases, Data Show
data.description: Marks & Spencer Group Plc’s grocery sales surged over the summer as the British retailer recovered from last year’s cyberattack, according to retail tracker Worldpanel by Numerator, Bloomberg reported.

data.title: Polymarket Bitcoin September 15 Breakout Bet Sees Sharp Drop in 78,000 Yes Odds
data.description: Polymarket’s "78,000" yes option in the Bitcoin September 15 breakout market fell sharply from 26.5% one hour earlier to 11.5%, a 15 percentage point swing. According to ChainCatcher, the move reflects sudden volatility in the prediction market and may be affected by breaking news.

data.title: Kakao Games To Acquire ME2ON For 98 Billion Won
data.description: According to The Korea Herald, Kakao Games is acquiring management control of social casino game developer ME2ON for about 98 billion won ($72 million) in its first major acquisition under a new ownership structure. The company said its board approved the purchase of a 39.56% stake in ME2ON, which will make Kakao Games the developer's largest shareholder and give it management control. Kakao Games said the deal is aimed at securing steadier earnings and expanding its global reach.

data.title: MediaTek Works With Customers To Optimize Mobile Chip Performance Amid Memory Supply Crunch
data.description: According to Nikkei Asia, MediaTek is working with customers to optimize the computing performance of its mobile chips as a memory chip supply crunch drives up component costs.

data.title: European Natural Gas Prices Supported as Market Remains Tight
data.description:
European natural gas prices remained supported as the market stayed tight. Wall Street Journal (Markets) posted on X, noting that supply conditions continued to underpin prices.

The article did not provide additional details on the drivers of the tight market or any broader outlook.

data.title: State Pension Likely to Rise by 3.9% Next April
data.description:
The UK state pension is likely to rise by 3.9% next April, according to the latest jobs and pay data, BBC reported. The increase would be set under the triple lock, which lifts the pension by the highest of average wage growth, inflation or 2.5%.

The Office for National Statistics said average wage growth between May and July slowed. It also said the number of vacancies in the UK shrank while the number of people claiming unemployment benefits rose.

data.title: STOCKS | Exxon Mobil Joliet Refinery Shuts Down After Power Outage
data.description: Exxon Mobil's Joliet refinery in Illinois was shut down after a power outage on September 13, interrupting gasoline and diesel production. According to Sina Finance, power was restored a few hours later, but the refinery still needs inspections and a gradual restart, and the company has not given a specific date for a return to normal production.
